budget_ms._comment: Budget includes interpreter startup. During active OneDrive sync + Defender scanning, startup alone consumes 1700ms+ (see interpreter_floor_ms). Values here are the p90 syncing-state total observed 2026-09-23.

_comment_interpreter_floor: Measured 2026-09-23 on Windows 11 / OneDrive (<org>) / Python 3.14.3. Method: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']) x20 from a running Python process — same spawn method as gates. Three states measured: (1) previous quiet session: min=403ms median=534ms max=618ms. (2) Active OneDrive sync post-commit: min=1343ms p50=1707ms p90=1930ms max=2640ms. (3) Full gate run under load: observed up to 4591ms. Root-cause finding: the floor elevation is system-wide — scripts in %LOCALAPPDATA% show similar or higher variance, so OneDrive file-read latency is NOT the bottleneck. Likely cause: Windows Defender scanning newly committed Python files. See FACTS.md §11.
_comment_kill_switch_headroom: Added to interpreter_floor_ms to get kill_threshold. 200ms covers stdlib imports (json/os/sys) before the CCMEM_DISABLED check. Extra headroom absorbs load amplification when running the full gate suite: multiple concurrent spawns drive system load higher than single-measurement floor. Total formula: floor(1700) + headroom(800) = 2500ms.
